key_concepts: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose
Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials; oxygen is released as waste
Chlorophyll in chloroplasts absorbs red and blue light and reflects green light
Leaves are the main site of photosynthesis
Xylem transports water, phloem transports food, and stomata allow gas exchange
Light-dependent reactions occur in thylakoids and produce ATP, NADPH, and oxygen
Water splitting supplies hydrogen ions and releases oxygen
The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma and fixes carbon dioxide into sugars
RuDP carboxylase catalyzes carbon fixation and PGA is converted to PGAL
PGAL is used to form glucose and other sugars such as fructose, sucrose, maltose, and star
Light, temperature, water supply, and carbon dioxide affect photosynthesis rate
